rows.name: dir?
rows.notes: Not defaulted, deliberately: left unset the resolved page direction governs, so a subtree inside an RTL region inherits instead of being reset to `ltr`.

rows.name: value?
rows.notes: Controlled. Always an array — single selection is an array of at most one.

rows.name: deselectable?
rows.notes: Whether clicking the selected item clears it. Defaults to `multiple`: a radio group has no deselect, and single mode *is* a radio group. Turning it on makes a nullable control, which is no longer the APG pattern.

rows.name: sizing?
rows.notes: `"equal"` cuts the track into equal columns, `"content"` sizes each segment by its own label; the pill is placed from a measurement of the active segment's layout box either way. A group can switch at runtime. A horizontal group wider than its room scrolls along its line; nothing folds.

rows.name: describedBy?
rows.notes: Ids of the text describing this control — a `field` supplies them.

rows.name: label?
rows.notes: The group's own visible name. The part is placed only when this is given — left out, nothing is added, and the group is named some other way instead (`aria-label`, a `Field`'s legend), exactly as the machine's own `hasLabel` read expects.

name: ToggleGroupOption
definition: Omit<CoreToggleGroupItemProps, "value" | "label"> & { readonly value: string; readonly label: string; }

rows.name: frame?
rows.notes: The outer box, which is the item of a flex or a grid parent: the layout of the group (`flex: none`, `align-self`, a width) goes here, while `className` and `style` on the group itself stay on the root.

rows.name: item?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY item, hence no `value`, `label` or `disabled` — the entry's own fields, excluded through `Own` the way `ToggleGroupItemProps` itself excludes them — and no `id` **or IDREF**: one id repeated down a group is a broken reference per segment, and one `aria-labelledby` repeated gives every segment the same name, which no dangling-IDREF check can see because the id it points at does resolve. `ref` goes for the same reason: a single ref held by N segments ends up holding the last one.
